name: California
nameStory: California is named after a fantasy novel. A 1510 Spanish romance described a mythical island called California, full of gold and ruled by Queen Calafia. Explorers thought Baja was an island, named it for the myth - and the place then actually turned out to have the gold.
capitalStory: Sacramento means 'sacrament' in Spanish. It sits where the Sacramento and American rivers meet, which made it the supply gate for the Gold Rush: Sutter's Mill, where gold was found in 1848, is only about 40 miles upstream.

majorFeatures.name: Central Valley
majorFeatures.note: Grows a quarter of America's food

funFacts: Mount Whitney (14,505 ft) and Death Valley (-282 ft), the highest and lowest points in the contiguous US, are about 85 miles apart.
If California were a country it would have roughly the fifth-largest economy on Earth.
It is the most populous state, with more people than all of Canada.
The General Sherman tree in Sequoia is the largest single living organism by volume on the planet.
whyItMatters: California's fire season now runs most of the year. Drought, a century of suppressing natural fires, and building into wild land have combined so that several of the state's largest fires on record have happened since 2017.
